sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Al–Ni binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AlNi-14Zhu.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L + (Ni) → Ni3Al, lies at 1643.1 K.
The Al–Ni system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as intermetallic rich, order disorder, congruent compound.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry (Hallstedt, 2025), which reproduces the assessment of J. Zhu, M.S. Titus, T.M. Pollock, J. Phase Equilib. Diffus., 35, 595-611(2014).
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Al reproduced by the dataset is 939.4 K.
The melting point of Ni reproduced by the dataset is 1728.2 K.
The dataset places a peritectic (L + (Ni) → Ni3Al) at 1643.1 K; the composition of L is x(Ni) = 0.759.
Eutectic equilibrium L → NiAl + Ni3Al is found at 1642.3 K and x(Ni) = 0.744 (L).
The dataset places a peritectic (L + NiAl → Al3Ni2) at 1412.2 K; the composition of L is a mole fraction of 0.261.
The peritectic reaction L + Al3Ni2 → Al3Ni is calculated at 1127.0 K, with L at x(Ni) = 0.160.
Peritectoid equilibrium NiAl + Ni3Al → Al3Ni5 is found at 973.4 K and x(Ni) = 0.625 (Al3Ni5).
We obtain 924.4 K for the eutectic reaction (L → (Al) + Al3Ni), where L has a mole fraction of 0.016.
Ni3Al melts congruently at 1643.1 K and x(Ni) = 0.761.
At 2000 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −49.27 kJ/mol, at x(Ni) = 0.500.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of NiAl at 298.15 K is −62.24 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
